thread:
Samir: quick FYI — onboarding CI for model `apex-small-v2` completed but we hit a subtle defaulting/fallthrough.
Samir: the schema validator marked the config as valid, but the runtime fell back to the global `max_input_length` instead of the model-level `config.max_input_length: 1024` we included. logs attached below.
devops-bot: build 3812 finished — tests: 412 passed, 3 warnings, 1 info
Samir: log snippet:
```
WARN runtime: config field `max_input_length` not found in final resolved config, falling back to pool.default.max_input_length (4096)
config provided: {"model": "apex-small-v2","tokenizer": {"pad_side":"right"},"config": {"max_input_length": 1024}}
```
Elena: hmm — so validator only checks schema shape but not inheritance/precedence rules. it accepted `config.max_input_length` but the runtime expects `model.max_input_length` (top-level) — that's a mismatch in our field aliases.
Mike: that's been a long-standing hole. schema has both `model.max_input_length` (deprecated) and `config.max_input_length` (new). validator currently treats them as separate optional fields; we need a rule: if both exist, error; if only new exists, map it to legacy path before runtime resolution.
Anya: I can take a small RFC + patch: add a `field_fallthroughs` section to the schema linter (explicit mapping + precedence), and make the CI fail if ambiguous aliases are present. pinging @Samir for example configs.
Samir: thanks @Anya — attaching the model config that triggered it.
```
{
  "model": {
    "name": "apex-small-v2"
  },
  "config": {
    "max_input_length": 1024
  },
  "tokenizer": {
    "pad_side": "right",
    "special_tokens_map": {
      "cls_token": "<s>",
      "sep_token": "</s>"
    }
  },
  "weights": "s3://redwood-models/apex/apex-small-v2/weights.pt"
}
```
Lucas: also noticed tokenizer quirk — our tokenizer onboarding step expects `special_tokens_map` keys `cls`/`sep` while some older models use `cls_token`/`sep_token`. that's another alias problem; runtime currently silently converts some keys but not all.
Elena: action items then: (1) linter: add alias mapping + ambiguity error; (2) runtime: make field mapping deterministic and log a single source-of-truth; (3) tokenizer onboarding: add small compat layer for `*_token` -> `*` keys and add a test vector.
Mike: +1. recommend linter change is gated behind a beta flag for one week so we don't break a large batch of in-flight onboards.
Anya: I'll open a PR with the linter change + CI rule. plan: add mapping table in schema config, add unit tests for both `apex-small-v2` config and a negative case.
Anya: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/412 — WIP
Samir: for the weights path: CI also flagged `s3://redwood-models/.../weights.pt` when we expect `weights.tar.gz` or a model manifest. can we add a small existence check (HEAD) in the CI step and a manifest parser step? the HEAD check would catch common typos.
Lucas: I'll add an S3 HEAD in the onboarding job; if HEAD returns 200 we'll proceed to manifest validation.
Elena: timeline: @Anya PR by EOD today, @Lucas s3-check in next deploy (tomorrow), Mike we'll roll the linter flag as beta for one week, then enable strict mode.
Samir: great. one more: please add a small note in the docs about preferred canonical keys (model.* vs config.*) so integrators don't accidentally create alias-only configs.
Anya: will add a short doc blurb in the PR description.
Mike: thanks all. closing loop — will add a CI card in the project board and tag the PR.
Samir: thanks — leaving this thread here for async followup :thumbsup:
